feature: The layers list only builds the rows you can see
summary: The layers panel now makes a row the first time you scroll to it. A document with a hundred and twenty layers builds six rows when the panel appears, where it used to build all one hundred and twenty. Nothing about the list looks or behaves different: it still hugs a short document, still caps and scrolls past the height you set, and a drag to reorder lands in exactly the same place.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next or Current alike (this is how the list draws, not what it does, so it is shared). No flags to turn on.

try.do: Open a new canvas and draw two rectangles.
Look at the Layers section: it should end right under the Canvas row, with no empty space before Position & Size.
Select a rectangle and press Command-D about a hundred times to fill the document up.
Watch the Layers section as the copies land: it should cap at five rows and start scrolling, not grow.
Scroll the layers list all the way to the bottom.
Check that Background and the Canvas row are the last two, with nothing cut off under them.
Scroll back up a screenful at a time and watch for a stutter as each new row appears.
Drag a row onto another to reorder it, and drag the grabber under the list to make the area taller.

evaluate: Scrolling a hundred-layer list: does each new screenful appear instantly, or can you catch a row arriving?
Does the list still stop exactly under the Canvas row in a short document, with no gap you notice?
Does the grabber under the list still track your cursor one to one, or does it lag or jump on the first pull?
Reordering by drag: does the blue drop line still appear where you expect, at the same moment it used to?
Is there anything about a long layers list that still feels slow, now that the rows are not the cost?
rough: Measured on the probe rather than assumed, same walk on both builds (Scripts/playtest/layers-lazy-rows-walk.json). Three layers: 3 rows built, before and after. A hundred and twenty layers: 120 rows built before, 6 after. Scrolling the whole list bottom to top builds 8 or 9 rows per screenful and costs a steady 23 to 28ms of main thread per screenful wherever you are in the list, so it does not get more expensive further down.

Behaviour checked by A/B rather than assumed: panel-reach-walk.json (row drag, the drop line above a row and inside a group, group disclosure, rows found by name) ran on both builds. Every step matched, and the screenshot of the panel after the drop is pixel for pixel identical.

The grabber under the list was NOT verified by a scripted drag, because no step can drag it. What was verified is the number it bases a drag on: the list's height is now worked out from the row count instead of measured, and the screenshots and the row positions in the panel inventory both say the worked-out number matches what is drawn. If the grabber feels different on the first pull, that is the thing to look at.

Left alone on purpose: the panel still asks for a thumbnail picture for every layer in the document, not just the rows on screen, so a hundred and twenty layer document still kicks off a hundred and twenty small background renders. Windowing that needs the scroll position and risks grey squares flashing past while you scroll fast, which trades an invisible win for a visible loss. Filed as its own task.

One consequence outside the app: a scripted walk can only reach a row that is built, so a walk naming a row far down a long list now has to scroll to it first. A new scrollPanel step does that, and the harness doc says so. Every existing walk works on documents short enough to fit the panel, and all of them still pass.
The synthesised scroll wheel is swallowed by the SwiftUI scroll area, so the new step scrolls the view directly instead and says so in its log line. That is a limit of the harness, not of the list.
